title: Power Pages: SDK for native mobile apps and kiosks
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap targets, existing Power Pages controls and general licensing are supported, and searches confirmed the narrowly stated SDK documentation gaps. Remove the unsupported suggestion that site-level controls were designed around the browser; the admin paths also need their final editing steps and the website-binding explanation needs a citation.

claims.quote: You can enable your site as a progressive web app (PWA), with native app–like look and feel, by using the Set up workspace in the Power Pages design studio.

claims.claim: A Power Pages site is a website.

claims.claim: The portals Web API requires its enabled site setting for each table exposed.
claims.quote: To enable the portals Web API for your site, configure the site settings for each table that you want to expose. Webapi/<table-name>/enabled: Enables or disables the Web API for <table name>.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Table permissions granted through associated web roles govern record access by the portals Web API.
claims.quote: The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated web role.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A table permission takes effect only when associated with at least one web role.
claims.quote: For a table permission to take effect, it has to be associated to one or more web roles. Users who belong to web roles are granted the privileges you select for the associated table permission.

claims.claim: The portals Web API is not optimized for third-party services or application integration.
claims.quote: The portals Web API is built for creating a rich user experience inside portal pages. It isn't optimized for third-party services or application integration.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects general Power Pages subscription capacity and pay-as-you-go options, not a published SDK-specific plan.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user capacity subscription license can be purchased for the anticipated number of unique, authenticated users. The Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages offers authenticated user capacity per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Power Pages has an anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of anonymous users who have accessed a website in a month.

claims.claim: The authenticated user meter measures unique authenticated users per website per month.
claims.quote: Meter Definition: Power Pages Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter: A measure of the number of unique authenticated users per website per month.

claims.claim: Anonymous website users are counted as unique users in a calendar month.

claims.claim: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings creates a site setting whose name and value configure Web API exposure.

claims.claim: mspp_name supplies the Webapi/<table-name>/enabled site setting name.

claims.claim: mspp_value supplies the site setting value true to enable the named table.

claims.claim: mspp_websiteid@odata.bind associates the new site setting with its website.
claims.quote: To associate new records with existing records when you create them, use the @odata.bind annotation to set the value of navigation properties.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/create-table-row to sources. Its 'Associate table rows on create' section supports @odata.bind; the already cited mspp_sitesetting reference identifies mspp_websiteid as the website navigation property.

claims.claim: Power Pages design studio > Security > Protect > Table permissions > table permission reaches the permission editor.
claims.quote: select Security. On the left pane in the Protect section, select Table permissions to view table permissions. Select the table permission that you want to edit
claims.fix: Keep the route 'Security > Protect > Table permissions > table permission' and add to the row note: 'In the permission editor, change the access type, privileges and applicable roles.' The cited edit procedure documents these final editing steps.
